subject: MAP: Load test scheduling & dedicated capacity sizing - next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: James Holden <james.holden@acmecorp.com>, Alice Morgan <alice.morgan@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 14:05:00 -0800
Subject: MAP: Load test scheduling & dedicated capacity sizing - draft and next steps

Hi James / Alice —

Thanks for the call today. As discussed, attaching an updated MAP (redwood-map-draft-v2.pdf) and a proposed traffic-replay schedule (traffic-replay-schedule.csv). Key items from our call: 

- Objective: Run a traffic replay + synthetic peak burst to validate dedicated capacity sizing and confirm latency at peak QPS.
- Target replay window: 24h of production traffic (Nov 15 00:00 - Nov 15 23:59 PST) with a focused peak QPS test at 18:00 PST for a 10-minute sustained burst.
- Peak QPS (ACME preliminary): you indicated ~1,200 sustained with 3k burst. Please confirm.
- Redwood responsibilities: provide replay harness, coordinate request routing to a dedicated pool, run pre-test dry run, and capture token-level latency/cost traces.
- ACME responsibilities: provide sanitized traffic export or a 24h traffic sample, confirm exact endpoint(s) to replay, and confirm authorised IP ranges for test.
- Dependencies: SOC2 evidence checklist (we have most items), and final procurement sign-off if Dedicated capacity is required.
- Target MAP milestone close: Nov 30, 2026 (to lock dedicated sizing and begin reserved capacity discussions).

Next steps: 
1) James — please confirm the peak QPS numbers and if the Nov 15 window works for you. Also send the sanitized traffic export or grant S3 access (we can accept a signed URL).
2) Aditya / Vivek — we should propose two capacity sizing options (standard dedicated pool for 1.5x average, and peak-optimized pool for 3k burst). Can you draft sizing by EOD tomorrow?
3) ACME procurement (Alice) — if Dedicated is chosen, procurement paperwork would start after sizing sign-off.

I've put the MAP milestone in the attached PDF and added owners. Happy to hop on a quick 30-min sync if useful.

Thanks,
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Sr. Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0182

From: James Holden <james.holden@acmecorp.com>

Cc: Alice Morgan <alice.morgan@acmecorp.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 09:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: MAP: Load test scheduling & dedicated capacity sizing - draft and next steps

Marissa — thanks for the clear recap and materials. Quick answers: 

- Peak numbers: our telemetry shows an average QPS of ~800 across the main inference endpoint with weekend peaks hitting ~2,400; sensible planning number for us is 1,200 sustained and 3,000 burst, so your outline is aligned.
- Nov 15 window: works for us, but procurement needs final confirmation (Alice cc'd) — they have a vendor blackout Nov 13-14, so Nov 15 is preferred.
- Traffic export: attaching a sanitized 24h sample (acme-sanitized-traffic-24h.jsonl). If you prefer S3 access, we can produce a signed URL — Alice, can you approve S3 access to redwood@acmecorp-s3?

We'd like Redwood to do a dry run on Nov 13 (non-peak) and the full replay + peak burst on Nov 15. If that timeline works, we'll lock it.

Thanks,
James
James Holden
Head of Platform Engineering | Acme Corp
james.holden@acmecorp.com

Attachment: acme-sanitized-traffic-24h.jsonl
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, James Holden <james.holden@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Alice Morgan <alice.morgan@acmecorp.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: MAP: Load test scheduling & dedicated capacity sizing - draft and next steps

Thanks James / Marissa — got the sanitized export. A few notes from the infra side: 

- We'll run a dry run on Nov 13 (09:00 PST) against a mirror dev pool to validate the replay harness and KV/prefix handling. No customer traffic will be affected.
- For capacity sizing: preliminary config options based on the sample:
  * Option A (Conservative): Dedicated pool sized for 1.5x average — target sustained QPS 1,200 — estimated 8 A100-equivalent units (config attached).
  * Option B (Peak-optimized): handles sustained 1,200 with 3,000 burst — estimated 14 A100-equivalent units with short-lived burst nodes and pre-warmed KV caches.
- We will collect token-level p50/p90/p99 latency and cost-per-1k tokens during the replay and the peak burst.
- Action: James — please share the exact endpoint paths we should rewrite during replay (we need to map URLs to the Redwood routing rule), and confirm any header auth we should strip/transform. Also list any IP allowlist entries.

I'll put the sizing numbers into the MAP PDF and send an update by EOD.

- Aditya
Aditya Rao
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.ai
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: MAP: Load test scheduling & dedicated capacity sizing - draft and next steps

Perfect — thank you all. Recap and owners (MAP milestone: Load/perf test scheduling):

- Deliverables & owners:
  1) Traffic export / S3 access: James / Alice (ACME) — deliver by Nov 12 EOD (received: sample delivered, full export requested).
  2) Dry run (non-peak): Redwood (Aditya) — Nov 13 09:00 PST.
  3) Full replay + peak burst: ACME + Redwood — Nov 15 18:00 PST (10-minute sustained burst).
  4) Capacity recommendations: Redwood (Aditya & Vivek) — provide Option A/B sizing and cost estimates by Nov 11 EOD (Aditya: sent sizing, will update MAP).
  5) Procurement sign-off (if Dedicated): Alice / ACME procurement — target Nov 30 MAP milestone close.

- Dependencies: final sanitized full export (ACME), IP allowlist, and SOC2 evidence (already in progress).
- Next sync: 20-min stand-up on Nov 12 16:00 PST if any open items. Otherwise we'll proceed with dry run on Nov 13.

I'll update the MAP PDF with the owners and close dates and re-share. Thanks for the quick turnaround.

Regards,
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Sr. Account Executive | Redwood Inference
